Team —

We need to lock decisions for the QBR packet on Wednesday. Finance gave us a tight headcount envelope and the executive agenda expects a clear recommendation on which reqs we prioritize, which backfills are mandatory, and where we need freeze/exception rationale.

Proposed approach (attached agenda + model):
- 60-minute wargame this afternoon to run scenarios (status quo, backfill-first, growth-first, conservative freeze)
- Each leader brings a one-slide rationale for 3 highest-priority reqs and 2 safe backfills
- Deliverable: one recommended plan and a list of 5 exception cases for the execs

Key ask: please review the headcount_model_v3.xlsx (attached) and the agenda PDF before 15:30. Bring any immediate redlines on compensation or procurement blockers.

Quick context: Ops and Platform have flagged two emergent backfills for infra and security that are critical to maintain SLAs; product asks for priority on two principal engineers tied to roadmap milestones. We need a defensible trade-off.

Thanks — I’ll circulate a facilitator script and we’ll record the session for QBR notes.

—Naomi

Naomi —

Thanks for pulling this together. I reviewed the model and added a second tab with two quick scenarios: one that preserves security/infra backfills (higher near-term cost) and one that converts one infra backfill into a contractor runway. High-level comments:

- Security backfill (Senior SecOps) is non-negotiable in my view — we lose compliance posture for SOC-related customers if we gap that role.
- The product principal engineers are high leverage but will push us into a higher comp band; suggest we package as "strategic hire" with a measurable milestone-based payout plan (link milestones to Q2 product OKRs).
- Consider a short-term hiring freeze exception for one senior data engineer to preserve the embedding production pipeline — risk: burst support costs if we patch with contractors.

I attached my excerpt of the model (headcount_model_v3.xlsx) with color-coded cells and a short note in cell comments. Happy to walk through during the wargame.

1) Any comp band moves above band 5 will require early sign-off from Finance (they need 7 business days for offer letters to account for rate approvals).
2) If we convert a backfill to a contractor, we must pre-approve a statement of work and vendor SOW routing — that will add ~10 days.

Operational ask: please flag in the agenda which hires are "time-sensitive" vs "nice-to-have" so procurement can prioritize routing. I marked time_sensitive in the model for the two infra roles.

Also: cross-team visibility request from CS — they want to be sure we don't cut capacity that will directly threaten the renewal pipeline in APAC. If we do freeze, include the customer-facing risk table.
